# Missa (usemissa.com)

> Missa is a free site where artists and writers find open calls, grants, residencies, magazines and prizes, see the fee, who can apply and the official page for each, and get reminded before they close. Organizations can post calls and take submissions through Missa. The public catalog, directory and rankings are open to everyone.

## Public pages

- [Browse open calls](https://www.usemissa.com/opportunities): open calls, grants, residencies, fellowships, contests, prizes, exhibitions and festivals.
- [Directory](https://www.usemissa.com/directory): residencies, literary journals, small presses, grant foundations and arts organizations.
- [Literary magazines](https://www.usemissa.com/journals): magazines and journals, with reading periods, fees and guidelines.
- [Residencies](https://www.usemissa.com/residencies), [grant funders](https://www.usemissa.com/grants) and [small presses](https://www.usemissa.com/presses).
- [Calls by country](https://www.usemissa.com/countries): open calls and publishers for each country, plus calls open worldwide.

## Guides

- [All guides](https://www.usemissa.com/guides): finding open calls and checking the fee, deadline and who can apply before you send work.
- [Where to find open calls: 10 sites compared](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/where-to-find-open-calls): Ten sites for finding open calls, from ArtConnect to Chill Subs, compared on price, fees shown, no-fee filters, reminders and tracking.
- [Free to apply isn’t always free: the fees an open call can charge](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/entry-fees-hanging-fees-participation-fees): Entry, hanging and participation fees and sales commission: when each one is charged, and how to find the full cost before you apply.
- [Duotrope alternatives for tracking your submissions](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/duotrope-alternatives): What Duotrope does best, what the free trackers cover, and how to move your submission history without losing any of it.
- [Literary magazine acceptance rates, and what they don’t tell you](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/literary-magazine-acceptance-rates): Where acceptance-rate numbers come from, what they say about The Paris Review and others, and how to use them without reading too much in.
- [How to apply to an artist residency](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/how-to-apply-artist-residency): What residency applications ask for, how to pick samples and write the proposal, and the windows and fees for seven programs.
- [Artist residencies with no application fee](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/free-artist-residencies): Find residencies that are free to apply to, and check what housing, stipends and travel really cover before you say yes.
- [Fully funded opportunities for artists and writers in Nigeria and Africa](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/fully-funded-opportunities-nigeria-africa): For artists and writers in Nigeria and West Africa: how to check eligibility, read “fully funded” and choose which calls to enter or watch.
- [The best literary magazines to submit to, by tier](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/best-literary-magazines-to-submit-to): What makes a magazine top tier, how rankings work, eleven magazines worth reading first, and how to order your submission list.
- [Submission fees and tip jars: when it’s worth paying to submit](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/literary-magazine-submission-fees): Reading fees, contest fees and tip jars: what each one buys, when to pay, and how to find magazines that read for free.
- [How to spot a scam open call or a vanity gallery](https://www.usemissa.com/guides/open-call-scams-vanity-galleries): How to check an open call or gallery invitation before you pay: the red flags, a ten-minute check, and what to do if you’ve paid.
- [Manuscript matcher](https://www.usemissa.com/discover/match): literary magazines that publish work like yours.
- [Magazine rankings](https://www.usemissa.com/rankings/magazines): the 2026 Missa literary magazine index.
- [Residency rankings](https://www.usemissa.com/rankings/residencies): artist residencies and fellowships ranked on funding, facilities and evidence.
- [How Missa works](https://www.usemissa.com/methodology): how Missa separates facts, scores and official sources.
- [About Missa](https://www.usemissa.com/about): what Missa is building and why.
- [Privacy](https://www.usemissa.com/privacy) and [Terms](https://www.usemissa.com/terms): the public privacy notice and terms.

## What Missa helps with

- Find open calls, grants, residencies, fellowships, contests, magazines, commissions and awards for the work you make.
- Check the deadline, fee, who can apply, location, what to send and the organizer's own page.
- Save calls, get reminded two weeks, a week, three days and a day before they close, and keep track of what you sent.
- Bring an existing submissions spreadsheet into the Tracker.

## Evidence and trust

- Missa keeps the official source close to the opportunity.
- Missa labels information that is unknown or conflicting.
- Missa does not silently fill in missing facts.
- The official host remains the authority for current requirements and applications.
- Saving an opportunity is not an application, and does not confirm eligibility.
